name: Michael Piseno

papers.title: Cloak: Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment Manipulation by Masking the End-Effector from the VLA
papers.abstract: We present Cloak, a training recipe that endows a vision-language-action policy with zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer by cloaking the end-effector from its own wrist camera. The mask comes for free from the robot's geometry and camera calibration, projected into the wrist view in real time with no generative model and nothing to hallucinate, and is augmented during training so the policy does not overfit to the end-effector's geometry. At deployment, we mask an unseen end-effector the same way and retarget its state and actions through two tips, the gripper jaws or a hand's fingertips, by inverse kinematics. We demonstrate the recipe with Cloak-VLA, fine-tuned on a single parallel-jaw gripper. Without new data or retraining, it transfers zero-shot to end-effectors it never saw, from another gripper to a five-fingered dexterous hand, at little cost to its performance on the source. Masking the wrist view is what unlocks this transfer: strong baselines given the same retargeting but no mask collapse on the unseen embodiments, most sharply on the dexterous hand.
